You can run an exhaustive query against an HNSW field by setting exhaustive to true in the vector query, which is useful for establishing ground truth. Quantization and smaller embedding dimensions further reduce memory at a small cost in recall.

questions.question: Filtered vector queries sometimes return fewer than k results, because the filter is applied only after the nearest neighbors are found. What should you set?
questions.explanation: vectorFilterMode controls when a $filter is applied in a vector query: preFilter, the default, applies the filter before the nearest neighbor search, so all k results satisfy the filter, while postFilter applies it after finding the top k neighbors, which can be faster but returns fewer than k results when the filter is selective. Some API versions also offer strictPostFilter for faceted scenarios. Filters on vector queries need filterable fields, and they are the standard way to apply metadata constraints such as category, date or security groups in RAG. For very selective filters, prefiltering keeps recall high.

questions.question: In keyword search results, newer documents and documents with higher popularity scores should rank higher. What should you add to the index?
questions.explanation: A scoring profile is an index-level rule set in Azure AI Search that boosts BM25 keyword relevance scores based on field weights (for example, matches in the title count more) and functions such as freshness (recent dates), magnitude (numeric values like popularity or rating), distance (geographic proximity) and tag matching. You can set a default scoring profile for the index or choose one per query with the scoringProfile parameter. In hybrid queries, scoring profiles affect the text portion before results are fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, and the semantic ranker reranks afterward based on meaning. Scoring profiles encode business rules about which documents should rank higher.

questions.question: Users search for 'PTO', but documents say 'paid time off', and keyword search misses them. What should you configure?
questions.explanation: A synonym map is an Azure AI Search resource that lists equivalent terms (for example PTO, paid time off and vacation) or one-way mappings, and you assign it to searchable string fields so keyword queries expand to include the synonyms at query time. Synonym maps use the Apache Solr format and can be updated without rebuilding the index. They improve recall for acronyms, jargon and product names in keyword and hybrid search, while vector search captures semantic similarity without explicit lists. Language analyzers and custom analyzers handle related needs such as stemming, stop words and tokenization for specific languages.

questions.question: During indexing, each chunk needs an LLM-generated summary and each image needs a text description (verbalization) produced by a chat model deployed in Foundry. Which skill should you use?
questions.explanation: The GenAI Prompt skill is an Azure AI Search built-in skill that calls a chat completion model deployed in Foundry with a prompt you define, to generate content during indexing, such as summaries, classifications, extracted facts or image verbalization (text descriptions of images that can then be embedded and searched). It takes inputs from the enrichment tree, such as chunk text or normalized images, and writes its output to a new enriched field. Because it calls an LLM for every document or chunk, it adds cost and indexing time, so use it where the enrichment clearly improves retrieval. The Azure OpenAI Embedding skill can then vectorize the generated text.

questions.question: For RAG ingestion of complex PDFs with tables and figures, which built-in skill does Microsoft recommend for layout-aware extraction and chunking in new pipelines?
questions.explanation: The Azure Content Understanding skill is an Azure AI Search built-in skill that uses Content Understanding to extract layout-aware content from documents, including text, tables, figures and structure, and to return semantically coherent chunks ready for embedding in a single step. Microsoft recommends it over the older Document Layout skill (based on Document Intelligence layout) for new RAG ingestion pipelines because it handles complex layouts, cross-page tables and figures with less configuration. Its output feeds index projections and an embedding skill that create chunk documents. Content Understanding usage is billed through the Foundry resource attached to the skillset.

questions.question: During indexing, you must run your own entity resolution logic hosted in an Azure Function. Which skill should you add to the skillset?
questions.explanation: The Custom Web API skill lets an Azure AI Search skillset call your own HTTP endpoint, such as an Azure Function or a container app, to run custom enrichment logic during indexing. The endpoint must implement the custom skill interface: it receives a JSON body with a values array of records, each with a recordId and data, and returns the same recordIds with output data plus any errors or warnings. You configure the URI, HTTP headers or managed identity authentication, timeout, batch size and degree of parallelism. The AML skill is the alternative for models hosted on Azure Machine Learning or Foundry endpoints.

questions.question: Enriched outputs such as entities, key phrases and OCR text must also be saved to Azure Storage tables for Power BI analysis, separate from the search index. What should you configure?
questions.explanation: A knowledge store is an Azure AI Search feature that persists enriched content from a skillset into Azure Storage, separately from the search index, for analysis and other downstream uses such as Power BI reports, data science or machine learning pipelines. It uses projections: table projections (rows in Azure Table Storage for analytics), object projections (JSON documents in blob containers) and file projections (images, such as normalized images, saved as files). A Shaper skill often builds the shape of the data before projection. Unlike index projections, which create searchable documents, knowledge store projections create stored data that isn't queried through the search index.

questions.question: An indexer that uses built-in AI skills such as OCR and entity recognition stops enriching after 20 documents each day. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Billable built-in skills in Azure AI Search, such as OCR, entity recognition, key phrase extraction, translation and image analysis, are processed by Azure AI services, so you attach a Foundry resource (an Azure AI services multi-service resource) to the skillset for billing. Without an attached resource, enrichment is limited to 20 free documents per indexer per day. Skills that call your own model deployments, such as Azure OpenAI Embedding or GenAI Prompt, are billed through those deployments instead. Utility skills such as Text Split, Shaper, Conditional and Text Merge are free.

questions.question: Your RAG pipeline must produce chunks of about 2,000 characters with 200 characters of overlap by using the Text Split skill. Which parameters should you set?
questions.explanation: The Text Split skill breaks text into chunks for embedding and retrieval: textSplitMode pages creates chunks up to maximumPageLength (measured in characters or tokens, depending on the unit setting) with pageOverlapLength of overlapping text between consecutive chunks, while sentences mode splits by sentence. Overlap preserves context across chunk boundaries, and a common starting point is chunks of a few hundred tokens with about 10 to 15 percent overlap. Chunks are then embedded with the Azure OpenAI Embedding skill and written as separate documents through index projections. For structured documents, layout-aware chunking with the Content Understanding or Document Layout skill usually outperforms fixed-size splitting.

questions.question: RAG answers must cite the source document title, URL and page number for every chunk they use. What must the ingestion pipeline do?
questions.explanation: Citation metadata, such as the source document title, URL or path, page number and section heading, must be captured during ingestion and stored as retrievable fields on every chunk, so retrieval results can be shown as citations and traced back to their source. Index projections copy parent fields (title, URL) into each chunk document, and layout-aware extraction supplies page numbers and headings for each chunk. Agents and the Azure AI Search tool need a retrievable URL field to produce clickable citations. Good metadata also enables filters, such as limiting retrieval to a department, date range or document type.

questions.question: You add an Azure Blob Storage knowledge source to a Foundry IQ knowledge base. What does the service create to ingest the content?
questions.explanation: Indexed knowledge sources in Foundry IQ, such as Azure Blob Storage, OneLake or indexed SharePoint, automatically generate a full Azure AI Search indexing pipeline: a data source, a skillset that cracks, chunks and vectorizes content (optionally with image verbalization or layout-aware extraction), an index and an indexer that keeps the content up to date. You choose the embedding and chat model deployments used for vectorization and verbalization when you create the source. The generated objects are regular search objects that you can inspect and tune. Remote knowledge sources, such as remote SharePoint and the web, instead query content at retrieval time without indexing it.

questions.question: A Foundry agent must retrieve grounding data from a Foundry IQ knowledge base. How does the agent connect to the knowledge base?
questions.explanation: A Foundry IQ knowledge base exposes an MCP endpoint, so a Foundry agent connects to it with an MCP tool (through a project connection that authenticates with the project's or agent's identity) and calls its knowledge_base_retrieve tool to run agentic retrieval. The knowledge base plans subqueries, searches its knowledge sources, merges and reranks results, and returns grounding data with references (or a synthesized answer), which the agent uses to answer with citations. The same knowledge base can serve several agents and can also be connected to Microsoft Copilot Studio. Agent instructions should say when to use the knowledge base and require citations of the returned sources.

questions.question: In Microsoft Agent Framework, relevant documents must be retrieved and injected into the agent's context automatically before every model call, without the model deciding to call a tool. What should you implement?
questions.explanation: A context provider in Microsoft Agent Framework is a component that runs around each agent invocation to add context, such as retrieved documents or memories, to the model's input before the call, and optionally to process the conversation afterward. Retrieval as a context provider guarantees grounding on every turn without relying on the model to call a search tool, while retrieval as a tool lets the model decide when and what to search, which saves tokens on turns that don't need it. Both patterns can use Azure AI Search or Foundry IQ as the backend. In deterministic workflows, retrieval can also be an explicit step whose output feeds the next agent or executor.

questions.question: Your organization builds agents in both Foundry and Microsoft Copilot Studio and wants one governed retrieval layer over the same content for all of them. What should you implement?
questions.explanation: A Foundry IQ knowledge base is a reusable, centrally governed retrieval layer built on Azure AI Search agentic retrieval, combining multiple knowledge sources with shared settings for retrieval reasoning effort, output mode and permissions. Because it is exposed through an MCP endpoint, the same knowledge base can be connected to Foundry Agent Service agents, Microsoft Copilot Studio agents and custom apps, so content is indexed once and governed consistently. Permission-aware retrieval and citations flow through to each agent's answers. Centralizing retrieval avoids duplicated indexes, inconsistent chunking and drift between agents.

questions.question: From varied business documents, you need text, tables, selection marks, paragraph roles such as titles and section headings, and document structure, but no specific business fields. Which Document Intelligence model should you use?
questions.explanation: The Layout model (prebuilt-layout) in Azure Document Intelligence extracts text, selection marks, tables, figures, paragraphs with roles (title, sectionHeading, pageHeader, pageFooter, footnote, pageNumber) and sections, each with bounding regions, and it can return the content as Markdown (outputContentFormat markdown), which is ideal for layout-aware RAG chunking. The Read model (prebuilt-read) is the lighter OCR option that returns pages, lines, words, paragraphs and detected languages for printed and handwritten text, and it can also produce a searchable PDF. Prebuilt models such as invoice, receipt, ID document, contract, bank statement, pay stub and US tax forms add business fields on top of layout. Document Intelligence v4.0 (API 2024-11-30) is the current GA version, used through DocumentIntelligenceClient in the azure-ai-documentintelligence SDK.

questions.question: Order forms from 30 vendors have different layouts, and the fields you need appear in different positions. Which custom Document Intelligence model type should you train?
questions.explanation: A custom neural model in Document Intelligence uses deep learning to extract labeled fields from structured, semi-structured and unstructured documents whose layouts vary, such as forms from many vendors, and it generalizes across layouts from a modest set of labeled samples. A custom template model suits fixed-layout forms where fields always appear in the same place, and it trains faster and supports many languages. You label documents in Document Intelligence Studio, train and test the model, and then call it by its model ID. Several custom models can be combined into a composed model, which in v4.0 uses a custom classifier to route each document to the right extraction model.

questions.question: One uploaded PDF contains an application form, a passport scan and a bank statement. Before extraction, you must split it into separate documents and identify each type. What should you use?
questions.explanation: A custom classification model (custom classifier) in Document Intelligence identifies the document type of each page or section and can split a multi-document file into separate documents, so each part can be routed to the right extraction model. You train it with labeled examples of each document class, and it handles mixed bundles such as loan packets or onboarding files. In Document Intelligence v4.0, composed models use an explicit classifier to route documents to their component extraction models. Content Understanding offers a generative alternative, with contentCategories and segmentation that classify and route documents to analyzers.

questions.question: With a Document Intelligence prebuilt model, you need two extra fields, such as PolicyNumber and EffectiveDate, without training a custom model. What should you use?
questions.explanation: Add-on capabilities extend Document Intelligence prebuilt models: queryFields (a premium add-on) extracts extra named fields that you list in the request without training a custom model, keyValuePairs extracts general key-value pairs, ocrHighResolution improves recognition of small text in large documents such as engineering drawings, formulas extracts mathematical formulas as LaTeX, styleFont detects font styles and handwriting, barcodes extracts barcodes and QR codes, and languages detects the language of text lines. You enable add-ons with the features parameter on the analyze request, and some carry extra charges. Query fields suit a few missing fields, while custom models remain better for many fields or complex documents.

questions.question: Invoices whose critical fields all have confidence above 0.9 must flow automatically into the ERP system, while the rest go to human review. What does this design rely on?
questions.explanation: Field confidence scores, from 0 to 1, returned by Document Intelligence and Content Understanding indicate how reliable each extracted value is, and comparing them with thresholds enables straight-through processing: documents whose critical fields all exceed the threshold flow automatically into downstream systems, while the rest go to human review. Thresholds should be set per field from evaluation data, balancing the automation rate against the cost of errors, with stricter thresholds for financial or legal values. Bounding regions (polygons) let reviewers see exactly where each value came from. Business validation rules, such as checking that line items sum to the total, catch errors that confidence scores miss.

questions.question: For RAG chunking with Document Intelligence, you need output that preserves headings, paragraphs and tables in a compact format that LLMs handle well. What should you request?
questions.explanation: Markdown output from the Document Intelligence Layout model (outputContentFormat set to markdown) represents a document's headings, paragraphs, tables, figures and selection marks in Markdown, preserving structure in a compact, LLM-friendly format. It enables semantic chunking by headings and sections, for example with a Markdown header splitter, which keeps related content together and improves retrieval. The JSON result still includes bounding regions and spans that link content back to pages for citations. Content Understanding's content extraction and RAG analyzers similarly return Markdown content for downstream reasoning.

questions.question: Thousands of documents in an Azure Blob Storage container must be analyzed with a custom Document Intelligence model, with results written back to storage, without managing thousands of separate operations. What should you use?
questions.explanation: Batch analysis in Document Intelligence v4.0 processes many documents in one request by pointing to a source Azure Blob Storage container (or a list of files) and a result container, and the service writes an analysis result for each document while you poll a single batch operation. It removes the client-side work of submitting and polling thousands of individual long-running analyze operations, and it works with prebuilt and custom models. Individual analyze calls (begin_analyze_document in the Python SDK) remain the choice for interactive, single-document scenarios. Storage access uses a SAS URL or the resource's managed identity.

questions.question: For RAG ingestion, one Content Understanding analyzer must return Markdown content, figure descriptions, a document summary and chunked output ready for embedding. Which analyzer should you use?
questions.explanation: prebuilt-documentSearch is the Content Understanding RAG analyzer recommended for document ingestion: it extracts content with layout as Markdown (paragraphs, tables and figures), generates detailed figure descriptions, represents charts in Chart.js syntax and diagrams in Mermaid syntax, produces a one-paragraph summary of the document and returns chunked output, with fixed-size or layout-aware semantic chunking, ready for embedding and vector indexing. It turns complex documents into clean, grounded text that LLMs and search indexes handle well. Figure analysis applies to PDF and image files. Content extraction analyzers (prebuilt-read, prebuilt-layout and prebuilt-digitalParse) provide OCR and layout without generative enrichment and need no language model.

questions.question: In Content Understanding output, how are charts in a document represented so an LLM can reason over their underlying data?
questions.explanation: Figure analysis in Content Understanding converts visual content into text that LLMs can reason over: charts are represented in Chart.js syntax, capturing the chart type, labels and data series, and diagrams such as flowcharts are represented in Mermaid syntax, while other figures get natural language descriptions. It is enabled with enableFigureAnalysis and enableFigureDescription on document analyzers (and is built into prebuilt-documentSearch), and it applies to PDF and image files. Formulas are extracted as LaTeX, and tables can be returned as HTML or Markdown (tableFormat). These representations make the numbers inside charts searchable and usable for grounded answers.

questions.question: Each field extracted by a Content Understanding document analyzer must include its page number, bounding box and a confidence score for review and citations. Which setting should you enable?
questions.explanation: Source grounding and confidence in Content Understanding are enabled with estimateFieldSourceAndConfidence on the analyzer (or estimateSourceAndConfidence on an individual field), which returns the source location (page number and bounding box) and a confidence score from 0 to 1 for each extracted field value. Fields that use the extract method require it, because extracted values must be traceable to the document. Grounding lets reviewers and agents verify values and cite their origin, and confidence scores drive straight-through processing versus human review. The returnDetails option adds further metadata, such as text spans and element positions.

questions.question: Data residency rules require that Content Understanding process your documents only within your resource's geography. What should you configure?
questions.explanation: Processing location is a Content Understanding setting that controls where the service may process your data: geography keeps processing within the resource's geography, dataZone allows processing within a broader data zone such as the United States or the European Union, and global allows processing in any region, which offers the most capacity. Stricter locations help meet data residency requirements, while broader ones can improve availability and throughput. Private endpoints and network rules are separate controls that restrict how clients reach the service, not where data is processed. Check model availability, because the models an analyzer uses must be deployable within the chosen boundary.

questions.question: Your documents are native digital PDFs and Office files, not scans. You need fast content extraction that reads each file's internal text and structure directly, without OCR. Which analyzer should you use?
questions.explanation: Content extraction analyzers in Content Understanding produce clean text and structure without a generative model: prebuilt-read provides OCR of words, paragraphs, formulas and barcodes, prebuilt-layout adds tables, figures, sections and hyperlinks, and prebuilt-digitalParse extracts machine-readable content directly from a digital file's internal structure and encoding, without OCR. digitalParse suits native digital documents, while scanned documents and photos need prebuilt-read or prebuilt-layout. Because these analyzers don't need language or embedding models, they are fast and inexpensive building blocks for RAG ingestion. In custom document analyzers, disabling OCR (enableOcr false) for native digital PDFs also improves performance.

questions.question: Invoices, receipts and purchase orders arrive mixed together, and each must be identified and sent to the right prebuilt extraction. Which Content Understanding analyzer should you use?
questions.explanation: Composed analyzers in Content Understanding classify an incoming document and route it to the right specialized analyzer: prebuilt-procurement handles procurement documents such as invoices, receipts, purchase orders, credit memos and utility bills, prebuilt-tax.us routes US tax forms, and prebuilt-mortgage.us routes mortgage documents. Domain-specific analyzers such as prebuilt-invoice, prebuilt-receipt, prebuilt-contract, prebuilt-idDocument, prebuilt-bankStatement.us and prebuilt-payStub.us extract predefined fields for a single document type. You can build your own routing with contentCategories (plus enableSegment to split multi-document files), with each category pointing to an analyzerId and an other category for anything that doesn't match. Routing first and extracting second keeps each schema focused and accurate.

questions.question: When you create a custom Content Understanding analyzer for PDFs, which property selects the parent analyzer whose defaults it inherits?
questions.explanation: An analyzer is the Content Understanding configuration that defines how content is processed and what output is produced, and a custom analyzer inherits defaults from the parent set by baseAnalyzerId, which must be one of four base analyzers: prebuilt-document, prebuilt-image, prebuilt-audio or prebuilt-video. The definition also includes config (options such as layout, OCR, figure analysis, segmentation and grounding), fieldSchema (the fields to produce) and models (completion and embedding model names, mapped to deployments configured as resource defaults). You create it with PUT /contentunderstanding/analyzers/{analyzerId}, which returns 201 Created with an Operation-Location header to track creation, and then call :analyze to process content. Copying a prebuilt analyzer as a template is a quick way to start a custom one.

questions.question: A custom Content Understanding analyzer extracts TerminationNoticePeriod inconsistently across contracts. What should you improve first?
questions.explanation: A field schema in Content Understanding defines each output field with a name, a type (string, number, boolean, date, object or array), a method (extract, generate or classify) and a description, and the description acts as a mini-prompt that tells the model what to look for and how to interpret it. Clear descriptions with definitions, formats, units and examples, such as the notice period in days required to terminate, given as a number, improve consistency more than any other change. Use enums with the classify method for fixed value sets, keep nesting to two or three levels, and require source and confidence for extracted values. Labeled examples added to a custom analyzer's knowledge base can further improve accuracy for difficult fields.

questions.question: A Content Understanding field must contain a short summary of a contract's renewal terms, written in the model's own words. Which method should the field use?
questions.explanation: Generation methods define how a Content Understanding field gets its value: extract returns a value that appears verbatim in the document, with source grounding and confidence; generate lets the model write a value, such as a summary, a normalized value or an inference drawn from several parts of the content; and classify picks one value from an enum. Use extract when values must be traceable and exact (invoice numbers, amounts), generate for summaries or derived insights, and classify for categories and policy labels. If no method is set, the service chooses one automatically, but setting it explicitly gives more predictable results. Generated values should be validated or reviewed when they drive important decisions.

questions.question: An agent must reason over the full content of long reports with their structure preserved, while a downstream database needs a few specific typed values. Which Content Understanding outputs should you use?
questions.explanation: Content Understanding analyzers return two complementary outputs: content, a Markdown representation of the document (or a transcript or description for other media) that preserves structure for LLMs, agents and RAG, and fields, structured JSON values defined by the field schema for databases, workflows and business rules. Agents benefit from Markdown because headings, tables and figure descriptions keep context, while systems of record need typed, validated field values. The omitContent option drops the content when only fields are needed, and returnDetails adds positions and spans for grounding. Designing outputs around their consumer (a person, an agent or a system) is a key part of analyzer design.

questions.question: You have sample documents of a new type and want Content Understanding to propose a starting field schema for a custom analyzer. Which analyzer should you run?
questions.explanation: Utility analyzers in Content Understanding help with analyzer design: prebuilt-documentFieldSchema analyzes sample documents and proposes an appropriate field schema that you refine into a custom analyzer, and prebuilt-documentFields extracts key-value pairs from documents and is used internally when input doesn't match a predefined schema. Starting from a proposed schema speeds up building analyzers for new document types. You still review field names, types, methods and descriptions, and test on representative samples before production. The Content Understanding experience in the Foundry portal lets you test and refine analyzers interactively.
